title: A PDF page is a decode source of the image component
scope:
admitting PDF to the image component's format roster as a decode-only source — the `open`
options that select a page and a scale, what `info` reports without rasterising, how the pixel cap
prices a page, what is refused rather than approximated, and the engine. Not in scope: PDF
*generation* ([0121](0121.md)); text extraction,
page manipulation and forms, which stay in the third-party channel (§ 5); the sandbox contract
([0003](0003.md)); the builder's plan/terminal shape and the component's entry points
([0120](0120.md) §§ 2–3, which gain
options here but no new member); scheduling — the second wave has no milestone, deliberately, like
the roster it joins.
dependsOnText:
[0120](0120.md) —
the pipeline, roster and cap this ADR extends; [0003](0003.md) — the sandbox that
makes shipping a PDF interpreter admissible at all.

summary.headline: A PDF page is an image you can open, not a program you run
summary.body:
`Image::open($bytes, {page: 3, dpi: 150})` rasterises one page of a PDF into the ordinary image
pipeline, and `Image::info($bytes)->frames` reports the page count without allocating a pixel.
The interpreter is pure Rust and runs inside the sandbox — replacing PHP's usual ImageMagick-to-
Ghostscript route, an unsandboxed interpreter with an exploit history long enough that
ImageMagick ships with PDF disabled. The page's size at the requested dpi is checked against the
pixel cap before any buffer exists. An encrypted file, a page out of range or an object the
engine cannot decode throws rather than rendering approximately.
